convention_rulings.topic: (d1) decision class of mixed options ('Approved as noted / Resubmit', 'APPROVED AS NOTED / RESUBMIT', 'Code B+Resubmit', 'B+R')
convention_rulings.ruling: Class 'approved as noted'; literal kept verbatim. The option or code leads with the approval (B / approved as noted) and the same legend offers separate revise-and-resubmit and rejection options that were not chosen. The reviewed version should record resubmission_required = yes on these rows so a scorer can tolerate a prediction that reports the resubmission condition.

convention_rulings.topic: (d2) authority approvals and marks that are not review decisions
convention_rulings.ruling: An authority's approval stamp or letter is class 'approved' when it carries no comments specific to the reviewed document: Civil Defence approved-plans stamp (literal = the stamp's own text only, a separate mark of unestablished authorship such as the yellow APPROVED box is noted, not joined; the issuer's own faint 'FOR INFORMATION ONLY' status is not a decision); du 'No Objection' without comments (with comments or written conditions it is 'approved as noted'; pre-printed 'refer to general conditions' footers are not comments); initial or conditional authority approval subject only to generic printed conditions (stage recorded in the note). A third-party pre-check stamp beside the authority decision is noted, not used. Not decisions (absent, no_decision_area unless a blank status area exists): an issuing authority's authentication of its own licence or certificate; company seals; contractor notes such as 'REVISED AS PER COMMENTS'; a contractor's restatement of a code on its reply sheet; a code combination quoted inside comment text about other submittals; receipt stamps. A dated stamp in an approval box without decision wording is 'ambiguous' with the actor recorded and is not resolved for scoring.
convention_rulings.evidence: Batches agree; no row changed by harmonisation.

convention_rulings.topic: (e) class of a code letter (C, D and others)
convention_rulings.ruling: The class follows the meaning of the code's printed legend, never the letter alone. The legend is read on the same page; if the page has none, the legend printed elsewhere in the same staged document (cover form or review block of the same package) applies; with no legend in the document, conventions section 5 applies (C = revise and resubmit, D = rejected). Mapping of legend wording: 'Approved' = approved; 'Approved as noted / with comments', 'Proceed as noted', 'No objection with comments' = approved as noted; wording that sends the document back for resubmission ('Revise & Resubmit', 'Incorporate comments & resubmit', 'Incomplete, Resubmit', 'Not Approved (Re-submit within 14 days)') = revise and resubmit; a plain refusal with no resubmission instruction in the option itself ('Not Approved', 'Rejected', 'Rejected Material') = rejected, and where one legend prints both a revise option and a separate rejection option, the rejection option is rejected even if it adds 'Resubmit'; deferral or information-only wording ('D - Deferment', 'Submitted for information') = other. A layout helper's letter mapping never overrides the printed legend. Consequences: EMAAR/Mirage C and D = revise and resubmit (F025 as ruled by B3); AREX and LACASA D 'Not Approved' = rejected; F035 p2 form D 'Deferment' = other. No current row is re-ruled: the only C rows are F011 (LACASA 'REVISE & RESUBMIT'), F025 (EMAAR C) and F072 (AREX C), all revise and resubmit; no D is marked in the pool.
convention_rulings.evidence: Batch rulings and their quoted legends; B7's 'D always rejected unless a legend is on the same page' and B4's 'C Not Approved (Re-submit) = revise and resubmit' are reconciled by the wording rule above.

convention_rulings.topic: (g) revision suffixes, labelled tails and revision values of another document
convention_rulings.ruling: (1) A tail on the page's own reference that carries its own 'Rev.' label ('B01-ASC-SD-ELE-0048-Rev.01') is a labelled revision, association resolved; identity is the number without the tail, and a scorer accepts either form. (2) An unlabelled suffix of the page's own printed number ('-R00', '- R02', 'B R1') is present with semantic_role 'suffix of the printed document number' and association uncertain (conventions section 4); at document level the field is resolved_for_scoring no and carries_fact no unless another in-scope page has a resolved revision. (3) A revision-like value that belongs to another document is never the page's revision: an attachment-table revision of an enclosed drawing, a suffix on an enclosed drawing's description line, a form or template code suffix ('P06/TRANS/R1'), and subject-line prose. The page revision is then absent (when the page has no own source) and the value is kept as referenced_revision or other identity. Counting the systematic LACASA/Scale '- R0n' suffixes would need an explicit owner convention change, not a per-row exception.

convention_rulings.ruling: A staged file holding several distinct documents is one pool document and counts once per field in the gate (conventions section 1). Truth is page-level: each in-scope page's field belongs to that page's own document. The file carries a field when at least one in-scope page has it present with association resolved (conventions section 7); pages whose state is ambiguous or illegible are not scored. A scorer must key on (pool id, page) and never score one file-level value against a compilation. B7's stricter 'all components share the same truth' is not adopted; it changes no row, because F069 has no page with a present, resolved identity under either rule.
convention_rulings.evidence: Batch rows for F002 (TAK and SAIFCO components), F035 (four other-project submittals), F069 (two quotations) and F043 (letter plus annex).

convention_rulings.topic: (h2) project or job number printed under a 'Reference' label
convention_rulings.ruling: When the value under a document's 'Reference' / 'Ref.' label is the project or job number, the identity is ambiguous (role not established), not present, and the number goes to other_identities. It counts as a project or job number when staged pages of the same project print it as such or distinct documents share it verbatim; file and folder names are never used.
convention_rulings.evidence: C:/t/r2x/r32-stage/renders/F062-p1.png ('Project ID'), renders/F068-p1.png ('Oracle Job No.'), as cited by B7.

convention_rulings.ruling: A readable value whose role, or choice among candidates, cannot be established is ambiguous; illegible is only for a value that cannot be read. A labelled revision cell that disagrees with the latest revision-table entry on the same page is ambiguous with both candidates and is not resolved for scoring; no inference from dates. A handwritten mixed outcome is ambiguous, transcribed as written. Ambiguous fields never count toward carries_fact.

A literal is the whole printed value, line breaks inside one value joined by one space, never a fragment ('ANNEXU RE B', not 'RE B'). Literals keep internal spaces, hyphens and glyphs as printed; where a space cannot be told apart from letter-spacing, or the same number is printed with and without it, the label keeps the printed form and the scorer compares whitespace-insensitively. The same printed literal on two different documents (F048 and F054, both 'FA-05') is two documents: the scorer keys on pool id, not on the literal.

Every region, whether drafted by hand or copied from a helper template, is checked against the page image. It is accepted when the value's centre lies inside the region widened by 0.01 page fraction (a slight clip of the value edge is tolerated); otherwise the ruling is 'correct' with the region fixed. A region-only correction changes no state, literal, class, association or document-field ruling.
convention_rulings.evidence: Batches agree (B1 tolerance 0.01, B5 slight clip tolerated, B7 region accuracy); no row changed.
